`publish()` sends a result to a destination named in `settings.yml`. This project has
one, `local`, a folder destination that writes to `published/` (ignored by git). Each
publish becomes a portable bundle with checksums and an offline `index.html` reader.
Run notebook 05 first: this one publishes its outputs.

```{python}
#| label: setup
import json

import framework as fw
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

root = fw.scaffold()
bp = fw.data_read("inputs.final.bp_analysis")
```

## The destination

The `publish` section names the destinations and the default. A relative folder `path`
is resolved from the project root, so this notebook (which runs from `notebooks/`)
still writes to `<root>/published`.

```{python}
fw.settings("publish")
```

## Publish a DataFrame

A DataFrame becomes a table artifact: the bundle keeps a CSV export and a typed
representation with column summaries. Look at the message with the version, and the
return value: the folder it landed in (or the URL, when the destination has a `url`).

```{python}
table = pd.read_csv(root / "outputs/tables/bp_by_visit.csv")

fw.publish(table, to="local", slug="bp-by-visit",
           title="Blood pressure by visit",
           description="Mean systolic and diastolic BP by arm and visit")
```

Without `to=`, `publish.default` picks the destination, so this goes to `local` too.

```{python}
fw.publish(bp.groupby("treatment")["systolic_bp"].describe().round(1),
           slug="bp-by-arm", title="Systolic BP by arm")
```

## Publish a figure, a model, and a file

A matplotlib figure is exported as SVG.

```{python}
means = bp.groupby(["visit_number", "treatment"])["systolic_bp"].mean().unstack()
ax = means.plot(marker="o", figsize=(6, 4), ylabel="Mean systolic BP (mmHg)")
fw.publish(ax.figure, slug="bp-trend", title="Systolic BP trend")
plt.close(ax.figure)
```

A fitted statsmodels model becomes a structured summary: coefficients and fit
statistics, never the data or a pickle.

```{python}
model = fw.load_model("bp_ols")

fw.publish(model, slug="bp-ols", title="OLS model of systolic BP")
```

A file on disk works the same way. Here, the PNG from notebook 05.

```{python}
fw.publish(root / "outputs/figures/bp_trend.png", slug="bp-trend-png",
           title="Systolic BP trend (PNG)")
```

## Publish a notebook

`publish_notebook()` renders a `.qmd` or `.ipynb` to HTML first, then publishes it.
This one renders `bp-brief.qmd`, so it takes a few seconds. No `title` is given, so the
title comes from the notebook's YAML: "Blood pressure brief".

```{python}
fw.publish_notebook(root / "notebooks/bp-brief.qmd", to="local", slug="bp-brief")
```

## Data files and folders

`publish_data()` and `publish_dir()` follow the same destinations and take a title and
description. `publish_data()` of a DataFrame becomes a table artifact, like `publish()`.
The slug comes from `dest`, folder part included: `tables/bp_by_visit.csv` becomes
`tables-bp-by-visit`.

```{python}
fw.publish_data(table, "tables/bp_by_visit.csv", title="BP by visit (data)",
                description="The bp_by_visit table as CSV")
```

`publish_dir()` publishes a folder as one artifact. `pattern` picks the files (a
regular expression on their paths); here only the SVG figures, from both the main
folder and the `meeting-2026-11/` subfolder. `dest="figures/svg"` becomes the slug
`figures-svg`.

```{python}
fw.publish_dir(root / "outputs/figures", dest="figures/svg", pattern=r"\.svg$",
               title="BP figures (SVG)")
```

`publish_list()` lists what the folder destination holds, one row per slug.

```{python}
fw.publish_list()
```

## A site-root folder destination

`settings.yml` has a second destination, `local-deck`, with `layout: site-root`.
Instead of a folder per artifact with versions, it keeps only the latest publish, at the
folder's root, which is what a GitHub Pages `docs/` folder or a single slide deck wants.
`to` picks it.

```{python}
fw.settings("publish.destinations.local-deck")
```

```{python}
fw.publish_notebook(root / "notebooks/bp-brief.qmd", to="local-deck")
sorted(p.name for p in (root / "local-deck").iterdir())
```

Publishing again replaces what's there, so `local-deck/index.html` is always the current
report. `publish_list()` shows the one artifact.

```{python}
fw.publish_list(to="local-deck")
```

## Versions

Publishing the same slug again adds a version. The latest sits at `published/<slug>/`
and every version is kept under `v/<number>/`.

```{python}
fw.publish(table, slug="bp-by-visit", title="Blood pressure by visit")
sorted(p.name for p in (root / "published/bp-by-visit/v").iterdir())
```

## What landed on disk

The site index lists every artifact. Open `published/index.html` in a browser to click
through the bundles; they work offline.

```{python}
site = root / "published"
pd.DataFrame(json.loads((site / "index.json").read_text()))
```

Each bundle has a manifest, `artifact.json`, with a checksum for every file.

```{python}
manifest = json.loads((site / "bp-ols/artifact.json").read_text())
{k: manifest[k] for k in ("slug", "title", "kind", "original", "generator")}
```

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(manifest["files"])
```

## What a folder destination refuses

Folder destinations have no access control, so passwords and unlisted links are refused
before anything is written.

```{python}
for options in ({"visibility": "unlisted"}, {"password": "s3cret"}):
    try:
        fw.publish(table, slug="never-written", **options)
    except fw.FrameworkError as error:
        print(options, "->", error)
```

## Framework Cloud and storage buckets

The remaining calls need a Framework Cloud login, a project token, or an S3 bucket.
This machine has none of those, and the tour stays offline. `cloud_status()` only reads
the local token store, so it is safe to run.

```{python}
connected = fw.cloud_status()
connected
```

Cloud publishing is skipped unless connected. With a login it would publish to
framework.pub (unlisted by default) and print the URL.

```{python}
if connected:
    fw.publish(table, to="cloud", slug="bp-by-visit", title="Blood pressure by visit")
    fw.publish_notebook(root / "notebooks/bp-brief.qmd", to="cloud")
else:
    print("Not connected: skipping cloud publishing. Run fw.cloud_login() to try it.")
```

Without a token or bucket these calls fail fast with a message that says what to set
up. Nothing is sent anywhere. (`to="s3"` asks for a plain bucket upload.)

```{python}
calls = {
    "ledger_list": lambda: fw.ledger_list(),
    "ledger_push": lambda: fw.ledger_push(),
    "cloud_settings": lambda: fw.cloud_settings(),
    "storage_test": lambda: fw.storage_test(),
    "publish_data to s3": lambda: fw.publish_data(table, "bp.csv", to="s3"),
    "publish_list to s3": lambda: fw.publish_list(to="s3"),
}
for name, call in calls.items():
    try:
        call()
    except (fw.CloudError, fw.FrameworkError) as error:
        print(f"{name}: {str(error).splitlines()[0]}")
```

These are not run at all, because they change your account or your machine's login:
`cloud_login()`, `cloud_logout()`, `cloud_sync()`, `skills_sync()`, and
`structure_import()`. Try them by hand once you are logged in.
